page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a virtual server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provisioned via 1 GB of network-attached local storage, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates strong processing and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and PassMark CPU evaluations, including physics and extended instruction sets. Multi-core performance is also highly rated, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 7141.83 GB/sec and large block uncached read speeds at 530.35 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Additionally, the system demonstrates high efficiency in data decompression, with single-threaded gzip compression at 40.49 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 555.02 GB/sec.

For workloads, the server is well-suited for memory-intensive general-purpose applications, database operations, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference, where it processes 135M model prompts at 5731.94 tokens/sec. However, the shared CPU allocation presents a potential performance tradeoff under sustained, simultaneous multi-core utilization. The minimal 1 GB of network-attached storage requires external storage solutions for data-heavy applications. From a resource density perspective, the instance offers high memory and core counts within a shared-resource framework, making it a cost-efficient option for large-scale parallel tasks that do not require dedicated CPU pinning.
